injuries.name: Martin Pospisil
injuries.note: After leaving Saturday's 4-3 overtime loss to Chicago late in the second period with an upper-body injury, Pospisil won't play against Ottawa on Monday. It's unclear when he will be ready to return, but he could be out for a while. Pospisil has a concussion history, and the Flames may take a cautious approach with his recovery.

injuries.name: Jonathan Huberdeau
injuries.note: Huberdeau played well in his first career AHL game. The 33-year-old is wrapping up the rehab process for his hip surgery. He can spend up to two weeks with the Wranglers on this conditioning loan, but if he continues to play well, he may not need the full amount of time before he's ready for his NHL season debut.

injuries.name: Kevin Bahl
injuries.note: Bahl suffered the injury in pregame warmups before Friday's 5-3 loss to Anaheim. He will finish the 2026-27 campaign with one goal, one assist, 12 shots on net, 16 blocked shots and 22 hits in 16 appearances. The Flames placed Bahl on injured reserve before Sunday's matchup against Philadelphia and recalled Brayden Pachal from AHL Calgary.

injuries.name: Gabe Perreault
injuries.note: Perreault is expected to miss the next 4-6 weeks, so it's not surprising to see the Rangers move him to IR. He has seven goals and 11 points in 24 appearances in 2026-27. Jaroslav Chmelar might serve in a middle-six capacity while the Rangers are missing Perreault.

injuries.name: Pavel Dorofeyev
injuries.note: Dorofeyev's status against the Sabres and Blackhawks on Wednesday and Friday, respectively, remains up in the air, but the fact that he is making the trip is certainly a step in the right direction. The 26-year-old winger has notched four goals and four assists, including a trio of power-play points, in his last 11 outings. Once given the all-clear, Dorofeyev should reclaim a middle-six role with the Rangers.

injuries.name: Oliver Bjorkstrand
injuries.note: Bjorkstrand landed on injured reserve Friday due to his upper-body injury, which has been revealed to keep him sidelined for the foreseeable future. Prior to going down, the 31-year-old winger compiled seven goals, 11 points, a plus-2 rating, 30 shots on net and 14 hits over 22 appearances. His current timetable for return should get him back in the mix around late January or early February. In the meantime, Matt Rempe will likely see more consistent playing time moving forward.

injuries.name: Alberts Smits
injuries.note: Smits landed on injured reserve in early November, which has caused him to miss the Rangers' last five games. The 18-year-old blueliner appeared in 17 contests prior to going down, where posted a minus-2 rating, eight shots on net, 16 hits and 10 blocked shots while averaging 14:29 of ice time. Given his current time line, he's expected to return sometime between late January and March. In his absence, Matthew Robertson and Scott Morrow should continue to see depth roles on the blue line.

injuries.name: Joe Veleno
injuries.note: Although Veleno didn't participate in practice Friday, it was encouraging to see him on the ice ahead of the session. The 26-year-old has been on long-term injured reserve since early October, and he was initially expected to miss approximately three months, so it wouldn't be surprising to see the Rangers bring him along slowly as he continues his recovery process.

injuries.name: Igor Shesterkin
injuries.note: Shesterkin was hurt during Friday's game against the Capitals when his right leg got jammed into the post while returning to the crease on a scrambled play, and the Rangers ruled him out for the season a day later. He was placed on injured reserve Sunday, and the team has now provided some clarification on the exact nature of his injury. Dylan Garand is slated to serve as the Rangers' No. 1 option in the crease until Joonas Korpisalo (lower body) is back in action.
